takeaways.text: Revenue dropped 10% to $11,589M, with declines in every geography: North America -11%, Europe, Middle East & Africa -13%, Greater China -4%, Asia Pacific & Latin America -7%, and Converse -15%. Nike Direct fell 13% as digital sales dropped 20%.
takeaways.title: Sales fell everywhere

takeaways.text: Gross margin rose 120 basis points to 45.4% on lower product, warehousing and logistics costs and earlier price increases — cushioning the revenue fall. Demand creation spending rose 15% to $1,226M around the summer sports calendar.
takeaways.title: Margins moved the other way

takeaways.text: Net income fell 28% to $1,051M and EPS 26% to $0.70; the tax rate jumped to 19.6% from 12.0% because the year-ago quarter had a one-time foreign-tax-credit benefit. Days before the report, Nike announced Elliott Hill would return as CEO on October 14, and postponed its Investor Day.
takeaways.title: A transition quarter

verdict: Nike's revenue fell 10% to $11.6B as sales declined in every region during its reset — but a richer gross margin limited the profit damage, and net income came in at $1.1B.
